 Judgment

This is a suit filed by the plaintiff for the relief of declaration that, the defendant has no authority to lay the pipeline in the suit schedule property and for permanent injunction to restrain the defendant, its official or anybody claiming through the defendant from interfering with the peaceful possession and enjoyment of the plaintiff over the suit schedule property.
2. The brief facts of the case of the plaintiff is that, he is the absolute owner, in possession and enjoyment of the suit schedule property bearing Sy.No.41/1, measuring 23 guntas, situated at Nagashettihalli Village, RMV II Stage, Bangalore North Taluk.
The suit schedule property was purchased by his grandfather late Dodda Munivenkatappa under a Registered Sale Deed dated 30.07.1931.
His grandfather died on 19.04.1992, leaving behind his only daughter Smt.Akkayamma.
The plaintiff is the only son of said Smt.Akkayamma, applied to CMC and BBMP for change of khatha in his name.
Earlier he paid tax to the Village Panchayath, then CMC, Byatarayanapura and now to the BBMP.

But in the Challans, the survey number was wrongly mentioned as Sy.No.40/1,
instead of Sy.No.41/1.
He formed a layout in the said property, built up houses, got electricity connection and let out to the tenants.
Though the defendant has no manner of right, title or interest on 13.11.2012, came to the suit schedule property and tried to dig the suit schedule property at the instigation of third parties.
The plaintiff has explained the details of the suit schedule property, then the Officials went away expressing their desire to come with much force and execute the earth work.
On 16.11.2012, with police force came to the suit schedule property and dig the suit schedule property, without any authority.
After verifying the records furnished by the plaintiff, Officials went out of the property and threatened that they would come again and execute the work.
But without acquiring the property, the defendant has no right to form the road or lay the pipeline in the suit schedule property.
Hence the plaintiff was constrained to file this suit for the afore mentioned reliefs.

3. In response to the suit summons, the defendant appeared through its standing counsel and the Assistant Executive Engineer, attached to BWSSB has filed his written statement and contended that, the suit for the relief of declaration is not maintainable as no notice was issued by the plaintiff under Section 126 of the Bangalore Water Supply and Sewerage Board Act (in short BWSSB Act).

entities.text: Bangalore Water Supply and Sewerage Board Act
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The alleged right, title and interest of the plaintiff over the suit schedule property is stoutly denied.

The allegation of the plaintiff that, either the BBMP or BWSSB or any other authority had not acquired the suit schedule property for formation of road or laying water pipeline etc., are all Sri.Venkatesh V vs The Commissioner on 12 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/57532475/
2 incorrect.
There exist a road in the suit schedule property connecting Devi Nagar to Kannuramma Layout.

In the said road, the defendant already laid the sanitary pipeline, on one edge of the road,
before institution of this suit.
Further, the BESCOM has already laid cables on this road.
The public are using the said road for their movements.

If the sanitary pipeline is not laid along with alignment,
it will not be possible to collect the sewerage generated from Devi Nagar for conveyance to sewerage treatment plant at Raja Canal.
The rain water or sewerage from the upstream side has to be conveyed to the downstream side through the natural slope.
Hence the defendant placed the sanitary pipeline on the existing road as per the topography.
Since the Board has already laid the sanitary pipeline before institution of this suit, the question of violation of court order does not arise.
The defendant made provision for water supply, sewerage and sewage disposal in Bangalore Metropolitan Area.
Accordingly, in the interest of public, the defendant has taken up the work in accordance with the BWSSB Acts and Rules.

The defendant may place and maintain sewers over,
under, along and across any immovable property whether within or without the local limits of the Bangalore Metropolitan Area, without acquiring the property.
Hence, in the interest of public, the Board can lay the sanitary pipes in the private property.
But in the case on hand, the Board laid the sanitary pipelines on the public road.
Hence the plaintiff is not entitled for any relief, much less the compensation.
Hence amongst other grounds prayed for dismissal of the suit with cost.

4. On the basis of the pleadings of the parties, my predecessor-in-office has framed the following issues and additional issue for determination:-
ISSUES 1.
Whether the plaintiff proves that he is in peaceful possession and enjoyment of the suit schedule property?
2. Whether the plaintiff further proves alleged interference by the defendant?
3. Whether the plaintiff is entitled for the relief sought for?
4. What Order or Decree ?

ADDITIONAL ISSUE 1. Whether the defendant proves that the plaintiff has filed his suit for relief of declaration, without issuing statutory notice to the defendant under Section 126 of BWSSB Act, as contended in additional written statement?
5.
In order to substantiate his case, the plaintiff alone has entered into the witness box as PW-1 and Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.23 were marked through him and closed his side.
On behalf of the defendant, the Assistant Executive Engineer, attached to BWSSB has entered into the witness box as DW-1 and Ex.D.1 to Ex.D.4 were marked through him and closed its side.

Sri.Venkatesh V vs The Commissioner on 12 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/57532475/
3 6.
Heard the arguments of the learned counsel for plaintiff and defendant.
The learned counsel for plaintiff also filed the written argument.

7. My findings on the above issues are as under:-
 Issue No.1: As per findings.
Issue No.2: In the negative.
Issue No.3: In the negative.
Addl. Issue No.1: As per findings.
Issue No.4:
As per final order below

for the following:
 REASONS 8. Issues No.1 & 2 and Additional Issue No.1:- Since all these issues are interconnected, taken up together for discussion to avoid repetition.

Initially, this suit was filed by the plaintiff for the relief of bare injunction to restrain the defendant from interfering with his peaceful possession and enjoyment over the suit schedule property.

Thereafter, he got amended the plaint and sought for the relief of declaration that, the defendant had no authority to lay the pipeline in the suit schedule property, without acquiring the land and without paying the compensation.

In para No.5 of the plaint, the plaintiff has taken contention that, on 13.11.2012 and 16.11.2012, the defendant came near the suit schedule property and made an attempt to lay the pipeline under the suit schedule property.
But he resisted their act with great difficulty.
9. The plaintiff in his examination-in-chief has reiterated the averments made in the plaint.
The documents marked on his behalf at Ex.P.1 is the Family Genealogical Tree.
Ex.P.2 is the Death Certificate of Dodda Munivenkatappa.
Ex.P.3 is certified copy of Sale Deed dated 30.07.1931.
Ex.P.3(a) is the typed copy of the same.
Ex.P.4 is the RTC Extract in respect of the suit schedule property, in the name of plaintiff.
Ex.P.5 is the Endorsement issued by the Police.
Ex. P.6
and P.7 are the copies of the Representation made by the plaintiff to the BWSSB.
Ex.P.8 to P.10 are the Tax Paid Receipts, in respect of property bearing Sy.Nos.40/1/1, 40/1/2 and 40/1/3.
Ex.P.11 is the copy of the Representation given by the plaintiff to the BWSSB.
Ex. P.12
is the office copy of the Complaint lodged to the Assistant Commissioner of Police, Yelahanka Sub-division, Bengaluru.
Ex.P.13 to P.15 are the Tax Paid Receipts in the Office of CMC, Byatarayanapura.
Ex. P.16
to P.19 are the Colour Photographs in respect of suit schedule property.
Ex. P.20
is the Pen Drive.
Ex.P.21 is the certified copy of Order Sheet of the proceedings initiated by the plaintiff against M/s.Kannuramma & Muneshwara Temple Trust before the Deputy Commissioner in R.P.No.274/2016-17.

Ex.P.22 and 23 are the Judgment and Decree passed in O.S.No.4568/2007 to show that, the suit instituted by the President of M/s.Kannuramma & Muneshwara Temple Trust against the plaintiff, in respect of the suit schedule property for the relief of possession and arrears of rent came to be dismissed.
10. In this suit, the defendant has taken multi-corner defence.
The first and foremost contention is that, as this suit was filed without issuing the statutory notice under Section 126 of BWSSB Act, this suit is liable to be dismissed.

Other contention taken by the defendant is that, much prior to Sri.Venkatesh V vs The Commissioner on 12 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/57532475/
4
institution of this suit, the defendant has laid the pipeline by the side of road formed in the suit schedule property.
Since the defendant laid the pipeline much prior to institution of the suit, suit for permanent injunction is not maintainable.
Further contended that, the Defendant Board was constituted for the public interest and it is required to lay the sewerage pipe as per Gravitational Force and topography of the land.

Further contended that, much prior to the institution of this suit,
the BBMP has formed the road and laid the electric cables by the side of the road.
As such, the defendant is not required to acquire the land to lay the pipe.
Further, stoutly denied the alleged right, title and interest of the plaintiff over the suit schedule property.
11. In his oral evidence, DW-1 has reiterated the averments made in the written statement.
The documents marked on behalf of the defendant at Ex.D.1 is the Letter of Authorisation issued by the Chief Engineer, BWSSB, authorising DW-1 to depose in this case.
Ex.D.2 is the certified copy of the Appeal Memo preferred before the Assistant Commissioner.
Ex. D.3
is the certified copy of the Order passed by the Assistant Commissioner.

Ex.D.4 is the certified copy of Record of Rights in respect Sy.No.41/1.
12.

Placing reliance on the pleadings and evidence, the learned counsel for plaintiff in his written argument has taken contention that, by virtue of the Registered Sale Deed, marked at Ex.P.3, the grandfather of plaintiff acquired the right over the suit schedule property.
In the Judgment and Decree passed in O.S.No.4069/1980, the suit schedule property had fallen to the share of his grandfather.
After the death of his grandfather, his mother Smt.Akkayamma being the sole surviving legal heir became the absolute owner of the suit schedule property.
The plaintiff being her only son became the owner of suit schedule property.
This being the factual position, the defendant has no authority to lay pipeline in the suit schedule property, without acquiring property and paying the compensation to the plaintiff.

13. In support of his argument, the learned counsel for plaintiff has relied on the decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Sukh Dutta Ratra and another Vs. State of Himachal Pradesh and others, reported in 2022 Live Law (SC) 347.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the said decision, the fundamental rights of an individual to protect his property has been discussed.

14. Further, the learned counsel for plaintiff relied on certain observations made by our Hon'ble High Court in the case of K.V.Srinivas Rao and others Vs. State of Karnataka and others (W.P.No.24580/2021).

entities.text: K.V.Srinivas Rao and others Vs. State of Karnataka and others (W.P.No.24580/2021)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Further argued that, as per Section 77 of the BWSSB Act, 1964, the defendant has every right to lay the pipeline in the property of private individual also, without initiating the acquisition proceedings.

Sri.Venkatesh V vs The Commissioner on 12 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/57532475/
5 16.

Further, the learned counsel for defendant drew the attention of this court with regard to the observations made by our Hon'ble High Court in the case of Sri.Narayanaswamy Vs. Bangalore Water Supply and Sewerage Board (MFA.No.8206/2015).

entities.text: Sri.Narayanaswamy Vs. Bangalore Water Supply and Sewerage Board (MFA.No.8206/2015)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In para No.3 of the said Judgment, it was observed as under;
"The learned Judge of Court below rejected IA No.1, referring Section 77 of the BWSSB Act.
The reasoning assigned by the Court below is found proper.
There is no good ground to interfere with the order passed by the Court below.
However, Sub Section (2) of Section 77 is available to the petitioner to invoke for seeking compensation for any damages."
17. This being the factual position, it is just and proper to reproduce the provisions contained under Section 77 of the BWSSB Act.

Same is read as under;
" Rights of user of property for sewers.

--
(1) The Board may place and maintain sewers over, under, along or across any immovable property whether within or without the local limits of the Bangalore Metropolitan Area, without acquiring the same, and may at any time for the purpose of examining, repairing, altering or removing any sewers enter on any property over,
under, along or across which the sewers have been laid:
Provided that the Board shall not acquire any right other than a right of user in the property over, under, along or across which any sewer is laid.

(2) In the exercise of the powers conferred upon it by this section, the Board shall cause as little damage as may be possible, and shall make full compensation for any damage caused by it."
18.
At this stage, I have gone through the observations made by our Hon'ble High Court in the case of Smt.Lakshmi Vs. The Chairman, BWSSB and another (W.P.No.20123/2014) .

entities.text: Smt.Lakshmi Vs. The Chairman, BWSSB and another (W.P.No.20123/2014)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the said proceeding, the notification of BWSSB regarding dig up and repair of sewerage line was questioned by the land owner.
The provisions of Section 77 of the BWSSB Act was brought to the notice of the Hon'ble Court.

At para No.12 of the said decision, it was held as under:
"In case any such damage is caused, the petitioner shall be free to approach the concerned Chief Engineer under Section 120 of the said Act of 1964 and the said Authority will decide the extent of compensation expeditiously not later than two months of the filing of the said claim and the Respondent BWSSB shall forthwith pay the same."
19.

Now it is clear that, BWSSB is a Special Enactment and as per Section 77, the defendant is having right to maintain sewers over, under, along or across any immovable property without acquiring the land.

Section 120 of the BWSSB Act makes it very clear that, any person aggrieved by any decision or Sri.Venkatesh V vs The Commissioner on 12 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/57532475/
6 order of the Water Supply Engineer or the Sanitary Engineer or other officer under the said Act or any rule or regulation made thereunder may within a period of sixty days from the date of such decision or order appeal to the Authority prescribed by the regulations and subject to revision by the Board.
Further, the orders of the Appellate Authority on such appeal shall be final.
Hence it is clear that, any exercise made by the defendant under the provisions of BWSSB Act is appealable.

20. That apart, as rightly contended by the defendant, as per Section 126 of the BWSSB Act, before got converting the suit for declaratory relief, the plaintiff not chosen to issue any Statutory Notice.
But in the instant case, the factual position is little bit different.

Initially, the suit was filed for the relief of bare injunction and subsequently, the suit was converted for the relief of declaration, by virtue of Order passed on the file of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in W.P.No.40838/2017.
Hence this court did not find any reason to go in detail with respect to the maintainability of this suit.
21. As stated supra, initially this suit was filed for the relief of bare injunction to restrain the defendant from laying pipes in any portion of the suit schedule property.
But the defendant has taken categorical contention that, much prior to institution of this suit, they have laid the pipes underneath the road portion of the suit schedule property.
Added to that, said road was formed by the BBMP and the concerned Authority also laid the electric cables underneath the road.
Looking to the cross-examination of PW-1 dated 21.10.2022, he has clearly admitted that, prior to institution of this suit, sewage pipe was laid by the side of the road.
That itself shows that, the plaintiff was very well knew about the laying of pipes by the side of the road as on the date of the suit.

Inspite of that,
he sought for an injunctive relief.

All these facts makes it very clear that, by suppressing the true facts this suit was filed and thereafter, sought for declaratory relief that, the defendant has no authority to lay water pipes underneath the suit schedule property.

22. Looking into the provisions contained under Section 77 of the BWSSB Act, it is crystal clear that,
without initiating acquisition proceedings, the defendant being an Authority, for the cause of public is having every right to lay pipeline in any of the property, either owned by the Government or private property.
Section 120 of the Act makes it clear that, there is an alternative remedy to the plaintiff to put forth his redressal.
With these observations, Issues No.1 and Additional Issue No.1 are answered as per findings and Issue No.2 in the negative.
23. Issue No.3:-
In this suit, the plaintiff sought for the relief of permanent injunction and declaration that, the defendant has no authority to lay pipelines in the suit schedule property.
But prior to institution of this suit, the pipes were laid by the side of the road formed in the suit schedule property.
As such, the relief of injunction sought by the plaintiff is not sustainable.
Further, as there is an alternative remedy, the plaintiff is not entitled for any relief as prayed for.
With these observations, Issue No.3 is answered in the negative.
24. Issue No.11:

In view of the above discussions, I proceed to pass the following:-
ORDER Suit of the plaintiff is hereby dismissed.

7 Parties are directed to bear their own cost.
